claims.text: scripts/up.sh does not start the API from the editor: it runs docker compose up --build, which builds the API from source per DonHang.Api/Dockerfile with the .NET 10 SDK on Linux, and the built API runs on Linux (aspnet:10.0 runtime).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: scripts/up.sh; DonHang.Api/Dockerfile (sdk:10.0 build, aspnet:10.0 final); docker-compose.yml api.build

claims.text: The api service publishes no port; from outside the lab it is reachable only through Caddy (plain HTTP :8080, and :8443 for donhang.local), which forwards /api/v1/* to api:8080.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: docker-compose.yml (api has no ports:, lab publishes 8080); Caddyfile handle /api/v1/* reverse_proxy api:8080

claims.text: docker-compose.yml gives the api three environment variables: ConnectionStrings__Default with Host=db, Jwt__SigningKey from .env (written by scripts/dev-secrets.sh), and ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT; appsettings.json has only Logging, AllowedHosts and Jwt Issuer/Audience.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: docker-compose.yml api.environment; scripts/dev-secrets.sh; DonHang.Api/appsettings.json

claims.text: Started without a ConnectionStrings:Default setting, Program.cs throws InvalidOperationException("ConnectionStrings:Default is not set") at startup, before it reads the signing key.
The host name db resolves only on the lab's network, not on the laptop.
claims.source_hint: docker-compose.yml networks (db hostname on the donhang network); Docker docs: networking

claims.text: Code that assumes Windows paths or a case-insensitive file system can fail on Linux, whose file systems are usually case-sensitive.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs: file path formats / cross-platform considerations

claims.text: curl -s http://localhost:8080/api/v1/products with the lab running returns a JSON list of products without sign-in.
A deploy has succeeded when the chosen version runs on the target and answers its users, not when files arrive; a working deploy proves the target was right at that moment only.
